Horizon uses certain radio bandwidths/frequency to communicate with us and back to New Horizons. The transmission takes a bit of time to reach us and back, radio frequencies are pretty fast, I'm not sure what ratio to the speed of tight that radio transmission travel though. Steveo in a reply to my comment clarified a bit, which you may understand better than my nonsense. Due to these limitations, activities such as sending a photo captured would probably be in the time span of days (so you can imagine how much better you have it with your wifi and 4g LTE. Engineers designed this in mind, they made sure to use frequencies that wouldn't be affected much by interference from space and earth's atmosphere, and the use of a highpowered transceiver on the craft pointed directly to massive satellites on earth doesn't hurt either. You can google New Horizons control system, I believe NASA has uploaded pictures of setup that controls the craft.

You're wifi signal is something I'm more familiar with (well wifi in general). There two parts of the equation, there is a router (the transmitter) and your wifi card (the receiver).

Now before anyone jumps and and try to correct, I know- technically both are transceivers (combined units in one) but for simplification- the router mainly acts as a transmitter and your wifi card acts as a transceiver. And yes, I also know that 'WiFi' is a brand name, just is only for those less tech savvy.

First, you want to turn your attention to your wifi router, you may have an outdated or just plain crappy router. Typically the more money you spend on one, the better results you tend to receive. Now that you decided its time to do yourself a favor and upgrade your internet connection- aim for a router around the $150+ price range. Usually you want something external antennas that stick out, do not cheap out on a router. Keep in mind that distance and the material that signal needs to pass through (between the walls) also heavily affect the signal. If you run into a situation where you think you need a better router than what's out there, look into professional access points instead of a consumer router. (Albeit they are very expensive.)

Second, if you have a poor low end laptop, or tablet, you probably have a cheap/poor quality wireless card. Since this device is used to pick up your wifi signal, you also want to make sure it's of good quality, or all your work up to this point is for naught. If you have a laptop for example, you can most likely replace the wireless inside of it, I recommend a decent intel wireless card which will run you around $40+. Sidenote, your wifi signal (if distance is your main problem) can be improved by a wireless extended, but be warned, one strong wireless router will beat out any wifi extender, and they are usually a pain to setup and manage.

If you have a proper setup, you will never have wifi problems. My router is on the first floor, and I'm in the basement, the signal goes through the concrete and several feet of dirt, but my signal never drops on any of my devices. If you plan according, do some research (computers/devices are never going to go away) and have good equipment, you won't have any issues well into the future. Education about wireless is really invaluable. This only covers a few basics, but there is more- networking is a very in-depth topic.

Your 4G LTE is similar, it's either that you're in an area with poor coverage, too many people on the network connected to the same tower, or your phone sucks. Not too much to do here, besides trying out different phones, or a different provider.

Edit: Clarified my post / rephrased a few things. Corrected 'Seed of Light' to 'Speed of Light', corrected other nonsense.
For a wifi router, I'd recommend an asus supported by shibby tomato firmware. More specifically the RT-AC66U.
Radio waves travel at the speed of light. The ratio is 100%.

More specifically, radio waves and light are both electromagnetic waves, just with different frequencies. Our eyes are sensitive to electromagnetic waves in the 'visible light' spectrum, but there is no fundamental difference other than the frequency range and no reason to think of them differently.
Oh okay, for some reason I thought it was a tiny fraction off, but that makes sense. Thanks for the clarification.

They use a 70 meter antenna with an equivilently massive reflector dish earthside, the piece on new Horizons is a 2.5m antenna, plus reflector dish with 2 12 watt amplifiers (for comparison, my wireless card is 14 milliwatts). It also only needs up or downlink, while the TCP protocol require both at the same time.

And for all that, the speed is 1 kbit/s (plus 4.5 hours latency for the light speed lag), which isn't strong enough to do much of anything with that you do with a phone.
